fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Rocky Terrain; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations: Providing clearly visible address identification at the main entry point could improve responder navigation, particularly given the single access point and extended driveway length. Marking or confirming the driveway entrance to support apparatus turning and staging decisions may assist personnel arriving under emergency conditions. Keeping the driveway clear of obstructions along its full length would support unimpeded apparatus movement toward the main building. Given limited rear access and adjacent rocky terrain, identifying and communicating any available secondary approach or staging area to local emergency services in advance could facilitate more effective operational positioning during an incident.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Fuel Continuity; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Heavy Brush; Wildland Interface; Long Driveway; Vegetation Adjacent to Access Route; Rock Outcrop
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the continuity of vegetation around the structure, particularly the brush observed in close proximity to the building, could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce opportunities for fire to reach the structure. Thinning or removing brush immediately adjacent to the structure and increasing separation between scattered trees, shrubs, and other vegetation within the near-structure zone may reduce fuel continuity across the property. Managing vegetation along the length of the driveway would support firefighter access and improve conditions for both ingress during suppression operations and egress during evacuation. Where scattered trees are present near the structure, maintaining vertical separation between lower branches and surface vegetation could further reduce fuel continuity. The rock outcrop present on the property represents a natural fuel break and its surroundings could be kept clear of encroaching brush to preserve and extend that benefit. Continued attention to vegetation management within the immediate structure perimeter and along the access route would support long-term wildfire resilience.
